brief_context: Author looking at load management and control schemes.
brief_extract:
Sally Fenner looks at schemes currently being evaluated by ESI engineers for
Load Management and Control
The Problem
How to make the most economical use of electricity generating capacity has been a constant problem for the Electricity Supply Industry. Because it cannot be stored, electricity has to be produced and distributed as and when the public and industry require it, and this means being geared to meet the peak demand periods and operating at under-capacity for a significant part of the 24-hour day — obviously a very uneconomic state of affairs.

brief_extract: Major studies have also been carried out in Sweden, the USA and Holland. brief_context: Switched on the generator at Burgar Hill opening ceremony.
article_title: POWER IN THE WIND: A promising source of electrical energy
brief_extract: The other development, pioneered in the USA, has been the use of advanced aerospace technology to reduce the mass and cost of large wind turbines, with the ultimate prospect of making the system cost effective even in areas of moderate wind. This 20m prototype horizontal wind turbine at Burgar Hill on Orkney which was set in motion on September 23 by Lord Avon will produce 250kW. In the background is an earlier smaller model.

title: Dr
brief_context: Explained the windy conditions and potential market for turbines.
article_title: POWER IN THE WIND: A promising source of electrical energy
brief_extract: The North of Scotland Hydro-Electric Board has provided funds for this project, which is being run by the Wind Energy Group (a consortium of Taylor Woodrow Construction, British Aerospace and GEC Power Engineering). At the opening ceremony when the generator was switched on by Under Secretary of State for Energy Lord Avon, Dr David Lindley, General Manager of the WEG, explained that Burgar Hill is one of the windiest places in the world with winds exceeding the minimum required to operate the generator occurring for almost three quarters of the year. The potential world market for wind turbines, he said, is in tens of thousands with a value measured in billions of pounds.

ERNEST SMITH retires

Ernest Smith, who retires this November after eight years as Office Administrator and Accountant, has been an integral and central figure of Headquarters staff, in contact with branch officers on financial affairs, handling the day-to-day administration of headquarters and staff, and administering the affairs of EAW Publications Limited. Before Mr Smith joined us in 1975 he had spent 35 years in the travel industry, plus war service in the RAF.
